identities.label: Poverty Point culture
identities.description: archaeological culture that inhabited the lower Mississippi Valley
identities.summary:
The Poverty Point culture is the archaeological culture of prehistoric indigenous peoples who inhabited a portion of North America's lower Mississippi Valley and surrounding Gulf coast from about 1730 – 1350 BC. They are named after their best-known archeological site.
Archeologists have identified more than 100 sites belonging to this mound-builder culture, who also formed a large trading network throughout much of the eastern part of what is now the United States.
